learning_outcomes.text: After successfully completing the module, students can describe the basic relationships of phase change and identify possible applications.

They can understand and explain hydro-, aerostatic and simple aerodynamic processes based on the conservation laws for momentum and energy, and analyze and calculate simple ideal and real flow processes.

Students who have successfully completed the "Applied Thermofluid Dynamics" module are able to design application-oriented, ideal processes and differentiate them with regard to their efficiency and identify alternative courses of action.

After successful completion of the module, students can analyze and evaluate simple thermodynamic and fluid mechanical problems. They are able to apply fundamental calculation methods to important thermal and fluid mechanical application examples and evaluate them computationally.

Successful graduates can physically correctly assess fundamental concepts of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics, evaluate their mathematical formulation and the underlying assumptions, and transfer them to new engineering tasks.

syllabus_topics: Applications to steady flow of incompressible fluids
assessment_rules: Graded assessment is a written exam. Ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of 2 experiments. Exam duration and scope are defined in the valid study regulations.
